newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran denies ambassador to Turkey left over row.
newsitem.headline: Iran denies ambassador to Turkey left over row.

text.p: Iran on Saturday denied reports that its ambassador had left Turkey over a diplomatic row sparked by his comments at an anti-Israel rally in favour of Islamic law, the official IRNA news agency said.

It quoted Deputy Foreign Minister Alaeddin Boroujerdi, as saying Ambassador Mohammad Reza Bagheri's tenure in Ankara had ended and that he would return to Tehran "at an appropriate time and after bidding farewell"
The Turkish foreign ministry said on Friday the ambassador and the consul had left the country on Wednesday.
Turkey protested to Iran early in February after the envoy spoke at an Islamist "Jerusalem Night" rally in an Ankara district along with the local mayor.
The speeches were blasted by the Turkish media as a call for the introduction of Islamic law, or sharia, in secular but Moslem Turkey.

A senior member of Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamist Welfare Party said earlier the ambassador's departure had nothing to do with the event. "His mission came to an end. He was leaving anyway," the MP said.
Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, visited Iran soon after forming a coalition with a conservative party eight months ago.
